article_title: Micro-credentials for Social Mobility in Rural Postsecondary Communities: A Landscape Report
citation: Tinsley, B., Cacicio, S., Shah, Z., Parker, D., Younge, O. & Luke Luna C. (2022, March). Micro-credentials for social mobility in rural postsecondary communities: A landscape report. Digital Promise. https://doi.org/10.51388/20.500.12265/151
title: KVEC stack of over 18 free competency-based micro-credentials hosted on the Digital Promise Micro-credential Platform
description: The Kentucky Valley Educational Cooperative, through a grant partnership with Digital Promise, created "a stack of over 18 micro-credentials focused primarily on the needs of students experiencing poverty, as well as special education populations." The credentials are free, competency-based professional learning opportunities for rural K-12 educators, hosted on the Digital Promise Micro-credential Platform and available to the public. Teachers leverage them to personalize continuing education credits and increase their rank, and schools adopt them whole-faculty or via team leads based on school data and student demographics.
requirements: State acceptance of micro-credentials for educator rank advancement, which in Kentucky came through a regulation change facilitated by a partnership with the State Board of Education
constraints: Kentucky requires four days of seat time for professional development, making it difficult to equate micro-credentials focused on demonstrating content knowledge rather than time spent
target_learners: Rural K-12 educators in southeastern Appalachian Kentucky
target_learning_goals: Understanding the needs of students experiencing poverty
Special education populations including hearing and visual impairment
examples: Some schools adopted micro-credentials whole-faculty based on strategic-plan data, while others used team leads so educators completed modules simultaneously and discussed findings together
key_sources: Tinsley, B., Cacicio, S., Shah, Z., Parker, D., Younge, O. & Luke Luna C. (2022, March). Micro-credentials for social mobility in rural postsecondary communities: A landscape report. Digital Promise. https://doi.org/10.51388/20.500.12265/151

article_title: What Makes Words Hard? Sakura at BEA 2026 Shared Task on Vocabulary Difficulty Prediction
citation: Adam Nohejl, Xuanxin Wu, Yusuke Ide, Maria Angelica Riera Machin, Yi-Ning Chang, Hitomi Yanaka. (2026). Sakura at BEA 2026 Shared Task 1: What Makes Vocabulary Difficult? https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14257
title: British Council Knowledge-based Vocabulary Lists (KVL) difficulty dataset
description: A large dataset of vocabulary difficulty scores for L1 Chinese, German, and Spanish learners of English, spanning thousands of vocabulary test items from the British Council's Knowledge-based Vocabulary Lists. Each test item consists of an equivalent L1 word, an L1 context, and a clue giving the first letter of the English word and its length in letters, targeting productive knowledge. Difficulty scores are intercept values of a generalized linear mixed model, i.e., the log-odds of a learner responding correctly, typically ranging from -5 to +5 with higher values easier.
requirements: Test items pairing an L1 word and context with a first-letter and length clue for the English word
Learner response data used to fit GLMM intercepts as difficulty scores
constraints: The article reports that difficulty scores are often affected by spelling difficulty and the construction of the test items in addition to genuine production difficulty, which could affect the utility of the dataset for other uses such as creating reading materials matched to the learner's level
target_learners: L1 Chinese, German, and Spanish learners of English
examples: Used as the training and evaluation data for the BEA 2026 Shared Task on Vocabulary Difficulty Prediction, with a fine-tuned XLM-RoBERTa model as the shared task baseline
key_sources: Adam Nohejl, Xuanxin Wu, Yusuke Ide, Maria Angelica Riera Machin, Yi-Ning Chang, Hitomi Yanaka. (2026). Sakura at BEA 2026 Shared Task 1: What Makes Vocabulary Difficult? https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14257
